cells.tense: You look at a tangled situation and the plain shape of it comes through clean.
cells.act: cut through the inertia with one decisive act
cells.ask: Once you've seen how something works, do one piece of it today. Rough counts. Don't study it further before you begin.
cells.core:
You can stand in front of something tangled and describe how it actually works — which parts move, what holds the rest up. You don't need the full history first, and you can usually hand someone the clear version they couldn't assemble themselves.

That half is running fine. What trails it is the moving: the shape gets named and then sits there, named, while the day goes on. Naming a thing and spending it are separate skills, and the second has been coasting on the first. Pick a pattern you've already seen clearly — three come to mind without effort — and carry it one crude step before tonight. Partial is fine; sloppy is fine. Staying put won't teach you what moving does.

cells.verb: taking in what is actually there and testing it with fresh questions

cells.tense: The reading is outrunning the evidence, and the conclusion lands before the situation does.
cells.act: ask the beginner's question about where to go
cells.ask: Take a thing you've filed as understood and put one plain question to it, the kind a newcomer asks, with the answer unknown.
cells.core:
Where you read patterns, you read them at speed — the whole shape of a situation arriving before anybody has finished explaining it. That has made you quick and hard to surprise. Lately it also means the verdict is in first, and everything after gets placed inside it. What the thing was going to show you arrives already sorted.

A bare structure can be a clean thing to hold, or a hiding place from the particular. One move tells which one you're in. Take something you've settled — a person, a job, a story you're sure you know — and put a beginner's question to it. Not a sharp one. A plain one. Something you'd ask if you'd walked in today and knew nobody's name. Don't go hunting for the answer.

cells.tense: Seeing how things work used to come without effort, and it has gone quiet for a stretch now.
cells.act: sense what has not happened yet, with wonder
cells.ask: Roam five unhurried minutes over something whose ending you don't know — no answer wanted, just sense what might come.
cells.core:
You used to catch what a situation was really doing — beneath the words, beneath the surface — and it landed without work. Lately the room is quiet. You look at the same situations and get the flat version, and you've stopped expecting anything more to arrive.

Straining at it won't help; leaning on a starved muscle only shows you it's starved. Put the attention somewhere with room in it instead. Something ahead that hasn't resolved — next season, next year, a question nobody's answered yet — and let yourself wonder about it. Not plan. Not solve. Feel toward what might be there and stay curious a while. Give that a handful of goes and plain sight comes back in its own season, pointed at what's actually near you.

cells.tense: You read rooms and people accurately most days, and none of it gets signed by you.
cells.act: make the fair call about a feeling, yourself
cells.ask: Keep a running page: each time you read a situation before anyone spoke it, jot a line and put your initials after it.
cells.core:
You catch what's passing between people before anyone speaks it — the shift in a room, the thing under what someone just told you — and it takes no effort. Then you do something with it: you say what softens the moment, you take the path that avoids the crash. From outside it reads as instinct. From where you're standing it reads as ordinary.

A fair reading of what's happening is a contribution, and your name has been left off it. The call is yours. You made it, and the way you then handle the person — what it costs them weighed against what it gives them — is not a small thing to be able to do.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that this person interrupts their own noticing with a plan or a demand before the pattern has finished showing itself — the record supports pattern-sight, not the impatience around it. A reader could reasonably say the problem is not hurry but that the pattern is obvious and nothing gets done about it, which is a different condition. All four asks survive that: waiting one beat, copying without deciding, following a thread for its own sake, and writing your own name on a read are useful whether the person is impatient or merely effective. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is the Balanced hinge as first drafted — 'the let-go is the whole of it' — which flatters the medicine; recast so the held shape is the point and the release is what it costs.
